# CASEs with `line` `readiness`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Readiness and slack** — what it takes to keep, reach and pay for capacities whose value lies in rare circumstances — readiness as response capability, slack and reconfiguration slack as different reserves, the resource threshold of a transition and its obstructions, and budget rules that remove options no one chose to give up (ADR-073). When transient support can be withdrawn is a line of its own (ADR-087).

| [CASE-315](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-315.md) v3 | Readiness simulator: spend-matching, carry-over | [LEAD-080](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-080.md) asked for A's simulator of [QUESTION-394](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-394.md) to be run twice, once with each month's budget set to the last month's peak spending ([CLAIM-577](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-577.md)) and once with carry-over, to see whether the heavy-rescue response of [CASE-213](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-213.md) stays reachable. The simulator has one or two squads, reported collisions of which a tenth need extrication, Poisson arrivals, a first-unit assessment right nine times in ten, travel from distance, mutual aid, skill that halves in about seven months without practice, and [CLAIM-577](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-577.md)'s capacity of 0.7 to hold and 1.3 with a squad out. Under spend-matching the squad is lost for good in every one of 300 runs, by a median of month 2 to 8, when it is sent only on confirmation or reports are few (two a month), and in 20 % of runs within nine years when it is sent provisionally to every one of six reports a month; drilling every month keeps it in every run. Rolling over the unspent part keeps it in every run; rolling over 60 % of it loses it as fast as spend-matching. [CASE-200](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-200.md)'s carry-over rule never loses it for good but, used every month, leaves it reachable in half the months. So the claim's prediction holds, and a quiet period turns out to mean a month in which nothing at all mobilizes the squad, not a month without a true need. The model is the assistant's and its rates are invented. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CASE-343](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-343.md) v2 | Maintenance-funding loop with decoupling | [LEAD-036](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-036.md) asked for [QUESTION-386](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-386.md)'s loop to be simulated with and without decoupling. A's model is run as the question records it, competence k decaying by δ and rebuilt by maintenance m bought from the budget above a holding cost, and the budget B̄ + η times observed activity, with the question's third process added: a capability is committed to an occasion with a chance that is zero below competence 0.4 and one above 0.8. Rarity is varied at fixed money, from one occasion in five years to sixteen a year, with η scaled so that a capability used on every occasion earns the same on average. Where the base budget alone sustains competence 0.25, below the commitment threshold, the coupled rule has an absorbing state, never committed and never funded, and over thirty years, under A's rule as written, reaches it in every run at one occasion in two and a half years or rarer, in 93 % at one a year, in 39 % at four a year and in under 1 % at sixteen. Funding maintenance apart from activity, at what full use would earn, never loses it at any rarity. Without the coverage feedback there is no absorbing state, though lumpy budgets still sustain less competence the rarer the use. Where the base alone sustains competence above the threshold, nothing is lost for good, but at the rarest occasions the coupled rule meets a quarter of them against nearly all under decoupling. The model is the assistant's and its rates are invented. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
